To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a novel approach to the synthesis and editing of videos is introduced; (2) the approach is based on a novel doubly autoregressive model for video synthesis; (3) the model uses contextual and ancillary information to improve the realism and controllability of the synthesis process; and (4) the approach is validated with experiments on standard datasets and tasks.
the synthesis of videos with controllable temporal continuity, spatial resolution, and realism is feasible with the proposed approach.

the proposed approach achieves a new state of the art in controllable video synthesis by combining a self-supervised approach with a doubly autoregressive prediction model, a learnable optical-flow module for enforcing spatio-temporal consistence, and a quantizer for handling ancillary information.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of new video sequences from old ones, conditioned on ancillary information, and we have developed a self-supervised approach to this task, with several novel contributions, that achieves state-of-the-art results in several benchmarks.
the synthesis of new video clips from old ones.
the problem of video synthesis from an existing video clip.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach achieves a good tradeoff between flexibility, controllability and quality, with the added benefit that it is fully self-supervised.
the CCVS approach provides a powerful and flexible tool for generating new videos from existing ones.
the proposed approach is a very good solution for the problem of video synthesis from old video, with several new and important elements for improved realism, controllability, and spatial resolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new approach for controllable video synthesis that is able to synthesize high resolution video sequences with a good temporal consistency.
we introduce a novel self-supervised learning framework for controllable video synthesis that is able to generate realistic and high-quality videos.
we propose a novel framework to synthesize new videos clips from given ones with high quality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with a little bit of extra effort, we can obtain much more realistic and controllable video synthesis than with previous methods.

a combination of self-supervision and controllable synthesis can yield a very powerful approach to video synthesis that outperforms previous approaches on several tasks and is easy to use and control.

the combination of several simple elements, including a novel doubly autoregressive model for forecasting and a novel optical flow module for enforcing temporal consistency, can yield very good results on video generation tasks, even when the training data is limited and the ancillary information is incomplete.
